overview: The Medford City Council Committee of the Whole met to review the Fiscal Year 2027 preliminary budgets for the Elections, Legislative, Fire, and Library departments. Councilors discussed critical staffing shortages, wage disparities, and disputed funding cuts with the city administration.

items.title: Elections Department Budget Review
items.summary: Elections Manager James Blatchford presented the department's budget, highlighting overtime increases for three upcoming elections and plans to introduce online census submission technology.

items.title: Legislative Department Budget Review
items.summary: The committee discussed the legislative budget, with councilors criticizing the administration for cutting technology lines and failing to fund a charter-mandated legislative aid position.

items.title: Fire Department Budget Review
items.summary: Chief Todd Evans and fire union representatives presented on extreme call volumes, severe staffing shortages, and injury-driven overtime costs. The committee approved a motion requesting a detailed breakdown of the professional services budget line, including litigation and arbitration expenses.

items.title: Library Department Budget Review
items.summary: Library Director Sam Sednick advocated for increasing the wages of underpaid part-time librarians and pointed out clerical errors in the administration's budget proposal. The committee approved a motion requesting an updated budget that includes a four-dollar-per-hour raise for part-time library staff.
